quick start

This page takes you through the first SDK call from scratch. Prerequisite: There is already a running ATOM software (atom_vp_interface service) and its address is known, such as http://127.0.0.1:10026.

Download the SDK

Download atom_sdk_<version>.zip from the Download Center and extract it locally. The archive is not OS-specific — it bundles all three languages, and the C++ SDK is pre-built for multiple platforms; pick the subdirectory matching your target platform after extracting.

atom_sdk_<version>/
├── cpp/
│   ├── linux-x86_64/
│   │   └── atom_sdk-<version>/
│   ├── linux-arm64/
│   │   └── atom_sdk-<version>/
│   └── windows-x64/
│       └── atom_sdk-<version>/
├── csharp/
│   └── AtomSdk.<version>.nupkg
└── python/
    └── atom_sdk-<version>-*.whl

In the installation steps below, <SDK_DIR> means the extracted atom_sdk_<version> directory. If the required version is not listed in the Download Center, confirm that it has been released.

General convention

  • All Service of SDK are accessed through the AtomClient unified entrance, and base_url is passed in during construction.

  • Picture operations are divided into editing state (GraphService/NodeService/GraphNodeService) and running state (RuntimeService). Which one to choose depends on Select the appropriate Service.

Python

1. Installation

# Optional: create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install the downloaded wheel
python -m pip install <SDK_DIR>/python/atom_sdk-<version>-*.whl

Dependencies: Python 3.10+, requests library (automatically installed with the package).

Verify installation:

from atom_sdk import AtomClient

client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026")
print("Installation successful,SDK ready")

Choose a wheel that matches your Python version and operating system. To change versions, download the corresponding archive from the Download Center and install it again.

2. First call

Let’s build the simplest graph from scratch and run it. There are 7 steps in total: Create client → Create graph → Open graph → Create node → Set parameters → Run graph → Release graph.

  1. Create client: AtomClient is the only entry to SDK, base_url fill in the host address and port number running the ATOM service, without adding a slash at the end.

    from atom_sdk import AtomClient

client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026")

  2. Create diagram:

    from atom_sdk import CreateGraphParams

result = client.graph.create_graph(CreateGraphParams("quickstart_graph"))
print("Diagram created successfully,status:", result["status"])

  3. Open the image: After opening, SDK will automatically cache timestamp returned by the server. All subsequent editing operations will automatically carry this version number, and there is no need to manually upload it. For details, see What is Timestamp.

    result = client.graph.open_graph("quickstart_graph")
print("Image is open,firstOpen:", result.get("firstOpen"))

  4. Add nodes to graph: this uses EpicProInput - it can read data directly from a local EpicRaw file, so you don’t need a real camera to try this out. Its image/pointCloud input ports are automatically bound as graph inputs when the node is created, so run_graph won’t fail with "no input bindings set".

    from atom_sdk import CreateNodeParams

result = client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("quickstart_graph", "EpicProInput"))
node_id = result["nodeId"]
print("Node created successfully,status:", result["status"], "ID:", node_id)

  5. Set node parameters: param_type has only two values - "init_params" (initialization parameters, loaded only once when the node is initialized, such as model path) and "run_params" (running parameters, effective every time it is executed). EpicProInput only has run_params, no init_params; for a node example with init_params, see Python parameter object.

    from atom_sdk import NodeParamUpdate

# Switch the data source to "read from a local file" instead of waiting for a real camera stream
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate("quickstart_graph", node_id, "input_method", "run_params", "inputFromFile")
)

# Point it at a local EpicRaw test file
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate("quickstart_graph", node_id, "epic_raw_path", "run_params", "/data/frame.epicraw")
)

    Replace /data/frame.epicraw with the path to your own EpicRaw test file. If the parameter value is a file, directly pass the pathlib.Path object, SDK will be automatically uploaded as multipart, and there is no need to manually read the file.

  6. Run the graph: run_graph automatically polls internally and waits for the graph execution to complete before returning.

    result = client.graph.run_graph("quickstart_graph")
print("Request status:", result["status"])
print("Run completed:", result.get("finish"))
print("Time consuming(ms):", result.get("total_time"))

  7. Release graph (optional): Release the graph after use and clean up server resources.

    client.graph.release_graph("quickstart_graph")
print("Image has been released")

3. Quick overview of error handling

SDK provides four exception types to accurately capture different types of errors:

Exception class Trigger scenario Key attributes

AtomSdkError

Base class for all SDK exceptions, catching them all

—

AtomHttpError

Network timeout, connection failure, HTTP 4xx/5xx

status_code

AtomApiError

The server returns a business error (image does not exist, parameter error, etc.)

status, payload

AtomTimeoutError

Graph running or node activation continues to be incomplete, SDK wait timeout

path, timeout_seconds, attempts, last_data

Minimal example:

from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError, AtomTimeoutError

try:
    client.graph.run_graph("quickstart_graph")
except AtomApiError as e:
    print(f"Server error(status={e.status}):{e}")
except AtomTimeoutError as e:
    print(f"Timeout waiting for interface to complete:{e.path}")

For a complete description of exception types, timeout_seconds behavior, and timestamp conflict retry policy, see Error handling and troubleshooting.

C++

1. Build configuration

Prerequisites: CMake 3.16+, a C+17 compiler (GCC 11, Clang 13+, or MSVC 2019+), and the system thread library; Boost is not required.

The extracted C++ SDK is at <SDK_DIR>/cpp/<platform>/atom_sdk-<version> (<platform> is one of linux-x86_64, linux-arm64, or windows-x64 — pick the one matching your target platform) and contains include and lib. No Conan remote or login is required.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(my_project CXX)

# The Windows package only ships a Release build; lock the configuration here.
# You still need to pass --config Release explicitly when building — omitting
# it fails at compile time with MSB8013 instead of crashing at runtime.
if(WIN32)
    set(CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES "Release" CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
endif()

# cpp/ is split into linux-x86_64/linux-arm64/windows-x64 subdirectories;
# auto-select the one matching the current build platform.
if(WIN32)
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "windows-x64")
elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "aarch64|arm64")
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "linux-arm64")
else()
    set(ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR "linux-x86_64")
endif()
set(ATOM_SDK_ROOT "<SDK_DIR>/cpp/${ATOM_SDK_PLATFORM_DIR}/atom_sdk-<version>")

find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

find_library(ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY
    NAMES atom_sdk_cpp
    PATHS "${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/lib"
    NO_DEFAULT_PATH
)

if(NOT ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Cannot find atom_sdk_cpp under ${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/lib")
endif()

add_executable(my_app main.cpp)
target_include_directories(my_app PRIVATE
    "${ATOM_SDK_ROOT}/include"
)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE
    "${ATOM_SDK_LIBRARY}"
    Threads::Threads
)

Build:

# Set ATOM_SDK_ROOT in CMakeLists.txt to the extracted SDK path first
cmake -S . -B build

# --config Release is required on Windows; omitting it fails with MSB8013
cmake --build build --config Release

2. Verify installation

// main.cpp
#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    std::cout << "C++ SDK ready" << std::endl;
    return 0;
}

C#

1. Installation

Prerequisite: .NET 6 SDK or later. The C# package is <SDK_DIR>/csharp/AtomSdk.<version>.nupkg; no additional NuGet source configuration is required.

Install the package from the local directory:

dotnet add package AtomSdk --version <version> \
  --source <SDK_DIR>/csharp

Or add in .csproj:

<PackageReference Include="AtomSdk" Version="<version>" />

Verify installation:

using AtomSdk;

var client = new AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
Console.WriteLine("C# SDK ready");

If the package cannot be found, confirm that <SDK_DIR>/csharp contains AtomSdk.<version>.nupkg and that --version matches the version in the file name.
